1.name: Sentinel Granodiorite
1.description: Coarse-grained, dark-gray, biotite-hornblende granodiorite with abundant sphene. Age about 93 Ma (K-Ar)

2.name: Talus
2.description: Rock waste derived from cliffs. Only especially extensive areas shown

3.name: Half Dome Granodiorite
3.description: Medium-grained biotite-hornblende granodiorite with conspicuous sphene. Locally porphyritic with abundant large phenocrysts of potassium feldspar

4.name: Granodiorite of Kuna Crest and similar rocks
4.description: Dark-colored, fine- to medium-grained, biotite-hornblende granodiorite with minor tonalite. Age about 88 Ma (U-Pb)

5.name: El Capitan Granite and similar Rocks
5.description: Coarse-grained, white to light-gray biotite granite and biotite granodiorite. Commonly porphyritic and blocky phenocrysts of potassium feldspar and conspicuous quartz grains. Age about 102 Ma (U-Pb)

6.name: Aplite and pegmatite
6.description: Dikes and small masses; mostly late differentiates of the Tuolumne Intrusive Suite

7.name: Alluvium
7.description: Stream deposits in major valleys and upland meadow areas; locally includes alluvial  fan deposits on the margins of major valleys and glacial outwash deposits

8.name: Tioga Till
8.description: Moraines usually sharp-crested with abundant boulders at surface

9.name: Pre-Tahoe Till
9.description: Moraines hummocky and dissected. Includes till mapped by some as Sherwin Till east of the Sierra Nevada crest

10.name: Tahoe Till
10.description: Moraines usually crested, but subdued, with scattered, weathered boulders at surface. Includes till mapped by some as Tenaya Till and Mono Basin Till east of Sierra Nevada crest

11.name: Metavolcanic rocks, undivided
11.description: Hornfels and other metamorphic rocks derived chiefly from sandstone, siltstone, shale, limestone, and conglomerate. Known to be of Jurassic age in Strawberry Tungsten Mine area near southeast corner of map area. Other bodies of rock assigned to this map unit are of questionable age

12.name: Diorite and gabbro
12.description: Occurs as generally small, irregular-shaped bodies throughout map area. Some bodies older and some younger than the plutonic rocks with which they are in contact

rule_notes: first match over major lithologies, then name, then description; volcanic with bottom age >= 145.0 Ma -> greenstone_metavolcanic; clastic sedimentary with bottom age <= 2.58 Ma -> alluvium; 'water' -> other
